title: HTTP/3 Low-Level Malformed Sequence Test Architecture
purpose: Define deterministic low-level HTTP/3 malformed sequence tests for RFC 9114 frame placement, control-stream sequencing, and message validation behavior.
design_summary: The low-level malformed sequence tests use a small custom test client inside the test project. The client drives the HTTP/3 frame reader, stream dispatcher, request message validator, and header validator directly so illegal stream and frame sequences can be generated without a normal HTTP client. Documentation records h3i-style examples for future live reproduction, while automated checks stay in-process and deterministic.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Unknown frame types are expected to be ignored by the HTTP/3 layer when permitted on the stream.
Reserved frame types are treated as unknown/grease and are expected to be ignored rather than rejected.
Malformed request sequencing and header validation failures map to the RFC 9114 application error codes exposed by the HTTP/3 layer.
PUSH_PROMISE sent by a client maps to H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED, while a server PUSH_PROMISE received before client MAX_PUSH_ID opt-in maps to H3_ID_ERROR.
The first slice does not require a live h3i installation or QUIC network scheduling.
risks: In-process malformed sequence tests do not prove full wire-level transport close behavior.
h3i command syntax and packaging can drift, so examples remain documentation until a future live h3i runner is pinned.
These tests are negative conformance checks and must not be converted into broad RFC 9114/RFC 9204 support claims.
